key_insight: Leaderboard scores on performance-optimization benchmarks can be misleading: they may reflect runtime noise, task-specific scoring quirks, and whether a benchmark is already saturated by public solutions, rather than true coding-agent capability. The paper argues for auditing these benchmarks before using them as evidence of progress.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the reliability problem in repository-level performance-optimization benchmarks for coding agents, where reported gains may not accurately measure real optimization ability.
method: Audits benchmark design and scoring for GSO, SWE-Perf, and SWE-fficiency.
Examines how runtime instability and benchmark-specific rules can alter leaderboard outcomes.
Analyzes how benchmark saturation from public submissions can distort apparent progress.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this paper is a warning that benchmark leaderboards may overstate model improvements. It encourages more careful evaluation practices and better benchmark design for measuring real-world coding-agent performance.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing benchmark patching and runtime comparison flow
Bar chart comparing leaderboard scores vs. adjusted reliability indicators
Warning icons highlighting runtime instability and scoring-rule sensitivity
Saturation heatmap showing how many tasks are already solved by public submissions
paper_title: Are Performance-Optimization Benchmarks Reliably Measuring Coding Agents?
paper_authors: Zhi Chen, Zhensu Sun, Yuling Shi, David Lo, Lingxiao Jiang
